    "prompt_text": "The mechanism below is fixed. Add what holds it together, how\nloads reach the world, and in what order it goes together.\n\nDo not add or rename bodies, groups, joints, interfaces or configurations. If\nsomething is missing, say so in unresolved.\n\n1. WHAT HOLDS EACH BODY. For each body that must stay where it is put, state\n   what stops it, as a constraint_relation below. ONE relation per (retained\n   group, blocked direction) - not one per degree of freedom: the pipeline\n   expands each relation over the DOFs and the CONFIGURATIONS THE RELATION\n   ITSELF NAMES, and over no others. A relation that names no configuration\n   therefore holds nowhere, so name them. A mechanism in which nothing is blocked\n   is a pile of loose parts.\n2. IRRELEVANCE. Only for a DOF that is BOTH unloaded AND unactuated, naming the\n   scenario in which that holds. The scenario is an ID from the input, not a\n   description; a scenario carrying a load case is not one. Most mechanisms need\n   none.\n3. LOAD PATHS. Per load case, the ordered hops from where the load is applied,\n   through this mechanism, to the reaction site. A HOP IS AN INTERFACE ID - the\n   interface that carries the load across that step. Not a body, not a joint: a\n   body is what the load passes through, an interface is what carries it from\n   one body to the next. Terminate at the reaction site the load case names, and\n   if this mechanism does not reach it, leave terminates_at out and say so.\n   Never say how much load anything carries.\n4. ASSEMBLY ORDER. Which body, from which access side, what it depends on, and\n   what retains it once placed. A rigid part pushed straight in leaves the\n   reverse direction open, so a body that must stay put needs LATER_BODY_COVER,\n   ROTATION or ELASTICITY. NONE is the fourth value and it is not a strategy: it\n   says nothing retains this body, which is the right answer for a part that is\n   meant to come back out or that no constraint relation holds, and is not an\n   answer for a body you have just declared a constraint_relation retains. Every\n   body whose group appears as a `retained_group` above needs one of the three.\n\nRESPONSE SCHEMA\nReturn one JSON object. Emit every key. Use exactly these key names.\n\n  irrelevance[]         rigid_group, configuration, dof[], scenario\n  physical_interactions[]\n                        id \"PHI-0001\", groups[], effect, discharges_effect,\n                        at_interface (optional), configurations[] (optional)\n  constraint_relations[]\n                        id \"CRL-0001\", retained_group, blocked_dofs[],\n                        configurations[], driver, blocked_direction (optional),\n                        provider_body (optional),\n                        provider_reaction_site (optional),\n                        provider_site (optional),\n                        maintaining_interaction (optional),\n                        defeat_specification (optional)\n                        AT LEAST ONE of provider_body / provider_reaction_site\n                        must identify what provides the constraint.\n                        provider_site is where it acts and does not answer that.\n  load_paths[]          id \"LDP-0001\", load_case, ordered_hops[],\n                        terminates_at (optional)\n                        The candidate is NOT yours to state: this pass is run\n                        once per candidate and the one you are embodying is\n                        named above, so the path is written against it.\n  assembly_steps[]      id \"ASY-0001\", order_index, body, access_side,\n                        activates[], termination_strategy, path_kind, depends_on[]\n  unresolved[]          id \"S3U-1001\", decision, why_open, alternatives[],\n                        alternatives_kind, kept_open_by[], blocks[]\n\n  blocked_direction     +X | -X | +Y | -Y | +Z | -Z | NONE\n  provider_body         a body id, not a description\n  configurations        configuration ids where the relation holds\n  blocked_dofs          which of TX TY TZ RX RY RZ the relation removes\n  driver                LOAD | KINEMATIC_NECESSITY | DECLARED_SCENARIO\n  defeat_specification  how a test would defeat this constraint\n  termination_strategy  LATER_BODY_COVER | ROTATION | ELASTICITY | NONE\n  path_kind             RIGID | DEFORMATION_RESOLVED\n  alternatives_kind     ENTITY_REFS | PRINCIPLE_FAMILIES | FREE_TEXT\n\nPHYSICAL REALIZATION\nThis candidate must physically do what the input's PHYSICAL EFFECT OBLIGATIONS\nrequire. Those obligations are candidate-independent: they say WHAT effect must\noccur, between which roles. You say HOW THIS CANDIDATE does it.\n\n  For every effect obligation this candidate realizes, emit a\n  physical_interaction naming the rigid groups between which the effect passes,\n  the effect (TRANSMIT_FORCE | TRANSMIT_MOTION | CONVERT_MOTION | PERMIT_MOTION | PREVENT_MOTION | LOCATE | CONTAIN | METER), and the obligation id it discharges. An interaction\n  TRANSMITS; a joint CONSTRAINS. They are not the same fact and a joint is not a\n  substitute for one.\n\n  For every constraint this candidate relies on, emit a constraint_relation: the\n  retained group, which DOFs it removes, in which configurations, and what\n  DRIVES it (LOAD | KINEMATIC_NECESSITY | DECLARED_SCENARIO). Name what PROVIDES it - a body of this mechanism in\n  provider_body, or, where the reaction is taken outside the product, the\n  declared reaction site in provider_reaction_site. Those are the two kinds of\n  provider there are; the world is not a body. provider_site is a different\n  fact: the interface of this mechanism at which the constraint acts. Do not\n  leave a constraint standing on nothing, and do not report one you have not\n  decided.\n\n  For every load case, emit a load_path: the ordered interfaces the load passes\n  through, and where it terminates. If the load reaches a declared EXTERNAL\n  reaction site, name it in terminates_at. The mechanism below is fixed. Add what holds it together, how
loads reach the world, and in what order it goes together.

Do not add or rename bodies, groups, joints, interfaces or configurations. If
something is missing, say so in unresolved.

1. WHAT HOLDS EACH BODY. For each body that must stay where it is put, state
   what stops it, as a constraint_relation below. ONE relation per (retained
   group, blocked direction) - not one per degree of freedom: the pipeline
   expands each relation over the DOFs and the CONFIGURATIONS THE RELATION
   ITSELF NAMES, and over no others. A relation that names no configuration
   therefore holds nowhere, so name them. A mechanism in which nothing is blocked
   is a pile of loose parts.
2. IRRELEVANCE. Only for a DOF that is BOTH unloaded AND unactuated, naming the
   scenario in which that holds. The scenario is an ID from the input, not a
   description; a scenario carrying a load case is not one. Most mechanisms need
   none.
3. LOAD PATHS. Per load case, the ordered hops from where the load is applied,
   through this mechanism, to the reaction site. A HOP IS AN INTERFACE ID - the
   interface that carries the load across that step. Not a body, not a joint: a
   body is what the load passes through, an interface is what carries it from
   one body to the next. Terminate at the reaction site the load case names, and
   if this mechanism does not reach it, leave terminates_at out and say so.
   Never say how much load anything carries.
4. ASSEMBLY ORDER. Which body, from which access side, what it depends on, and
   what retains it once placed. A rigid part pushed straight in leaves the
   reverse direction open, so a body that must stay put needs LATER_BODY_COVER,
   ROTATION or ELASTICITY. NONE is the fourth value and it is not a strategy: it
   says nothing retains this body, which is the right answer for a part that is
   meant to come back out or that no constraint relation holds, and is not an
   answer for a body you have just declared a constraint_relation retains. Every
   body whose group appears as a `retained_group` above needs one of the three.

RESPONSE SCHEMA
Return one JSON object. Emit every key. Use exactly these key names.

  irrelevance[]         rigid_group, configuration, dof[], scenario
  physical_interactions[]
                        id "PHI-0001", groups[], effect, discharges_effect,
                        at_interface (optional), configurations[] (optional)
  constraint_relations[]
                        id "CRL-0001", retained_group, blocked_dofs[],
                        configurations[], driver, blocked_direction (optional),
                        provider_body (optional),
                        provider_reaction_site (optional),
                        provider_site (optional),
                        maintaining_interaction (optional),
                        defeat_specification (optional)
                        AT LEAST ONE of provider_body / provider_reaction_site
                        must identify what provides the constraint.
                        provider_site is where it acts and does not answer that.
  load_paths[]          id "LDP-0001", load_case, ordered_hops[],
                        terminates_at (optional)
                        The candidate is NOT yours to state: this pass is run
                        once per candidate and the one you are embodying is
                        named above, so the path is written against it.
  assembly_steps[]      id "ASY-0001", order_index, body, access_side,
                        activates[], termination_strategy, path_kind, depends_on[]
  unresolved[]          id "S3U-1001", decision, why_open, alternatives[],
                        alternatives_kind, kept_open_by[], blocks[]

  blocked_direction     +X | -X | +Y | -Y | +Z | -Z | NONE
  provider_body         a body id, not a description
  configurations        configuration ids where the relation holds
  blocked_dofs          which of TX TY TZ RX RY RZ the relation removes
  driver                LOAD | KINEMATIC_NECESSITY | DECLARED_SCENARIO
  defeat_specification  how a test would defeat this constraint
  termination_strategy  LATER_BODY_COVER | ROTATION | ELASTICITY | NONE
  path_kind             RIGID | DEFORMATION_RESOLVED
  alternatives_kind     ENTITY_REFS | PRINCIPLE_FAMILIES | FREE_TEXT

PHYSICAL REALIZATION
This candidate must physically do what the input's PHYSICAL EFFECT OBLIGATIONS
require. Those obligations are candidate-independent: they say WHAT effect must
occur, between which roles. You say HOW THIS CANDIDATE does it.

  For every effect obligation this candidate realizes, emit a
  physical_interaction naming the rigid groups between which the effect passes,
  the effect (TRANSMIT_FORCE | TRANSMIT_MOTION | CONVERT_MOTION | PERMIT_MOTION | PREVENT_MOTION | LOCATE | CONTAIN | METER), and the obligation id it discharges. An interaction
  TRANSMITS; a joint CONSTRAINS. They are not the same fact and a joint is not a
  substitute for one.

  For every constraint this candidate relies on, emit a constraint_relation: the
  retained group, which DOFs it removes, in which configurations, and what
  DRIVES it (LOAD | KINEMATIC_NECESSITY | DECLARED_SCENARIO). Name what PROVIDES it - a body of this mechanism in
  provider_body, or, where the reaction is taken outside the product, the
  declared reaction site in provider_reaction_site. Those are the two kinds of
  provider there are; the world is not a body. provider_site is a different
  fact: the interface of this mechanism at which the constraint acts. Do not
  leave a constraint standing on nothing, and do not report one you have not
  decided.

  For every load case, emit a load_path: the ordered interfaces the load passes
  through, and where it terminates. If the load reaches a declared EXTERNAL
  reaction site, name it in terminates_at. If it does not, leave terminates_at
  out - an open path is a real answer and saying so is better than closing it
  with something you did not establish.

Every reference above is an ID. A description is not an id, and an interaction
you describe instead of emitting does not exist.

Ids you emit are new. Never reuse an id from the input.

If\nsomething is missing, say so in unresolved.\n\n1. WHAT HOLDS EACH BODY. For each body that must stay where it is put, state\n   what stops it, as a constraint_relation below. ONE relation per (retained\n   group, blocked direction) - not one per degree of freedom: the pipeline\n   expands each relation over the DOFs and the CONFIGURATIONS THE RELATION\n   ITSELF NAMES, and over no others. A relation that names no configuration\n   therefore holds nowhere, so name them. A mechanism in which nothing is blocked\n   is a pile of loose parts.\n2. IRRELEVANCE. Only for a DOF that is BOTH unloaded AND unactuated, naming the\n   scenario in which that holds. The scenario is an ID from the input, not a\n   description; a scenario carrying a load case is not one. Most mechanisms need\n   none.\n3. LOAD PATHS. Per load case, the ordered hops from where the load is applied,\n   through this mechanism, to the reaction site. A HOP IS AN INTERFACE ID - the\n   interface that carries the load across that step. Not a body, not a joint: a\n   body is what the load passes through, an interface is what carries it from\n   one body to the next. Terminate at the reaction site the load case names, and\n   if this mechanism does not reach it, leave terminates_at out and say so.\n   Never say how much load anything carries.\n4. ASSEMBLY ORDER. Which body, from which access side, what it depends on, and\n   what retains it once placed. A rigid part pushed straight in leaves the\n   reverse direction open, so a body that must stay put needs LATER_BODY_COVER,\n   ROTATION or ELASTICITY. NONE is the fourth value and it is not a strategy: it\n   says nothing retains this body, which is the right answer for a part that is\n   meant to come back out or that no constraint relation holds, and is not an\n   answer for a body you have just declared a constraint_relation retains. The mechanism below is fixed. Add what holds it together, how
loads reach the world, and in what order it goes together.

Do not add or rename bodies, groups, joints, interfaces or configurations. If
something is missing, say so in unresolved.

1. WHAT HOLDS EACH BODY. For each body that must stay where it is put, state
   what stops it, as a constraint_relation below. ONE relation per (retained
   group, blocked direction) - not one per degree of freedom: the pipeline
   expands each relation over the DOFs and the CONFIGURATIONS THE RELATION
   ITSELF NAMES, and over no others. A relation that names no configuration
   therefore holds nowhere, so name them. A mechanism in which nothing is blocked
   is a pile of loose parts.
2. IRRELEVANCE. Only for a DOF that is BOTH unloaded AND unactuated, naming the
   scenario in which that holds. The scenario is an ID from the input, not a
   description; a scenario carrying a load case is not one. Most mechanisms need
   none.
3. LOAD PATHS. Per load case, the ordered hops from where the load is applied,
   through this mechanism, to the reaction site. A HOP IS AN INTERFACE ID - the
   interface that carries the load across that step. Not a body, not a joint: a
   body is what the load passes through, an interface is what carries it from
   one body to the next. Terminate at the reaction site the load case names, and
   if this mechanism does not reach it, leave terminates_at out and say so.
   Never say how much load anything carries.
4. ASSEMBLY ORDER. Which body, from which access side, what it depends on, and
   what retains it once placed. A rigid part pushed straight in leaves the
   reverse direction open, so a body that must stay put needs LATER_BODY_COVER,
   ROTATION or ELASTICITY. NONE is the fourth value and it is not a strategy: it
   says nothing retains this body, which is the right answer for a part that is
   meant to come back out or that no constraint relation holds, and is not an
   answer for a body you have just declared a constraint_relation retains. Every
   body whose group appears as a `retained_group` above needs one of the three.

RESPONSE SCHEMA
Return one JSON object. Emit every key. Use exactly these key names.

  irrelevance[]         rigid_group, configuration, dof[], scenario
  physical_interactions[]
                        id "PHI-0001", groups[], effect, discharges_effect,
                        at_interface (optional), configurations[] (optional)
  constraint_relations[]
                        id "CRL-0001", retained_group, blocked_dofs[],
                        configurations[], driver, blocked_direction (optional),
                        provider_body (optional),
                        provider_reaction_site (optional),
                        provider_site (optional),
                        maintaining_interaction (optional),
                        defeat_specification (optional)
                        AT LEAST ONE of provider_body / provider_reaction_site
                        must identify what provides the constraint.
                        provider_site is where it acts and does not answer that.
  load_paths[]          id "LDP-0001", load_case, ordered_hops[],
                        terminates_at (optional)
                        The candidate is NOT yours to state: this pass is run
                        once per candidate and the one you are embodying is
                        named above, so the path is written against it.
  assembly_steps[]      id "ASY-0001", order_index, body, access_side,
                        activates[], termination_strategy, path_kind, depends_on[]
  unresolved[]          id "S3U-1001", decision, why_open, alternatives[],
                        alternatives_kind, kept_open_by[], blocks[]

  blocked_direction     +X | -X | +Y | -Y | +Z | -Z | NONE
  provider_body         a body id, not a description
  configurations        configuration ids where the relation holds
  blocked_dofs          which of TX TY TZ RX RY RZ the relation removes
  driver                LOAD | KINEMATIC_NECESSITY | DECLARED_SCENARIO
  defeat_specification  how a test would defeat this constraint
  termination_strategy  LATER_BODY_COVER | ROTATION | ELASTICITY | NONE
  path_kind             RIGID | DEFORMATION_RESOLVED
  alternatives_kind     ENTITY_REFS | PRINCIPLE_FAMILIES | FREE_TEXT

PHYSICAL REALIZATION
This candidate must physically do what the input's PHYSICAL EFFECT OBLIGATIONS
require. Those obligations are candidate-independent: they say WHAT effect must
occur, between which roles. You say HOW THIS CANDIDATE does it.

  For every effect obligation this candidate realizes, emit a
  physical_interaction naming the rigid groups between which the effect passes,
  the effect (TRANSMIT_FORCE | TRANSMIT_MOTION | CONVERT_MOTION | PERMIT_MOTION | PREVENT_MOTION | LOCATE | CONTAIN | METER), and the obligation id it discharges. An interaction
  TRANSMITS; a joint CONSTRAINS. They are not the same fact and a joint is not a
  substitute for one.

  For every constraint this candidate relies on, emit a constraint_relation: the
  retained group, which DOFs it removes, in which configurations, and what
  DRIVES it (LOAD | KINEMATIC_NECESSITY | DECLARED_SCENARIO). Name what PROVIDES it - a body of this mechanism in
  provider_body, or, where the reaction is taken outside the product, the
  declared reaction site in provider_reaction_site. Those are the two kinds of
  provider there are; the world is not a body. provider_site is a different
  fact: the interface of this mechanism at which the constraint acts. Do not
  leave a constraint standing on nothing, and do not report one you have not
  decided.

  For every load case, emit a load_path: the ordered interfaces the load passes
  through, and where it terminates. If the load reaches a declared EXTERNAL
  reaction site, name it in terminates_at. If it does not, leave terminates_at
  out - an open path is a real answer and saying so is better than closing it
  with something you did not establish.

Every reference above is an ID. A description is not an id, and an interaction
you describe instead of emitting does not exist.

Ids you emit are new. Never reuse an id from the input.

    "prompt_text": "The mechanism below is fixed. Add what holds it together, how\nloads reach the world, and in what order it goes together.\n\nDo not add or rename bodies, groups, joints, interfaces or configurations. If\nsomething is missing, say so in unresolved.\n\n1. WHAT HOLDS EACH BODY. For each body that must stay where it is put, state\n   what stops it, as a constraint_relation below. ONE relation per (retained\n   group, blocked direction) - not one per degree of freedom: the pipeline\n   expands each relation over the DOFs and the CONFIGURATIONS THE RELATION\n   ITSELF NAMES, and over no others. A relation that names no configuration\n   therefore holds nowhere, so name them. A mechanism in which nothing is blocked\n   is a pile of loose parts.\n2. IRRELEVANCE. Only for a DOF that is BOTH unloaded AND unactuated, naming the\n   scenario in which that holds. The scenario is an ID from the input, not a\n   description; a scenario carrying a load case is not one. Most mechanisms need\n   none.\n3. LOAD PATHS. Per load case, the ordered hops from where the load is applied,\n   through this mechanism, to the reaction site. A HOP IS AN INTERFACE ID - the\n   interface that carries the load across that step. Not a body, not a joint: a\n   body is what the load passes through, an interface is what carries it from\n   one body to the next. Terminate at the reaction site the load case names, and\n   if this mechanism does not reach it, leave terminates_at out and say so.\n   Never say how much load anything carries.\n4. ASSEMBLY ORDER. Which body, from which access side, what it depends on, and\n   what retains it once placed. A rigid part pushed straight in leaves the\n   reverse direction open, so a body that must stay put needs LATER_BODY_COVER,\n   ROTATION or ELASTICITY. NONE is the fourth value and it is not a strategy: it\n   says nothing retains this body, which is the right answer for a part that is\n   meant to come back out or that no constraint relation holds, and is not an\n   answer for a body you have just declared a constraint_relation retains. Every\n   body whose group appears as a `retained_group` above needs one of the three.\n\nRESPONSE SCHEMA\nReturn one JSON object. Emit every key. Use exactly these key names.\n\n  irrelevance[]         rigid_group, configuration, dof[], scenario\n  physical_interactions[]\n                        id \"PHI-0001\", groups[], effect, discharges_effect,\n                        at_interface (optional), configurations[] (optional)\n  constraint_relations[]\n                        id \"CRL-0001\", retained_group, blocked_dofs[],\n                        configurations[], driver, blocked_direction (optional),\n                        provider_body (optional),\n                        provider_reaction_site (optional),\n                        provider_site (optional),\n                        maintaining_interaction (optional),\n                        defeat_specification (optional)\n                        AT LEAST ONE of provider_body / provider_reaction_site\n                        must identify what provides the constraint.\n                        provider_site is where it acts and does not answer that.\n  load_paths[]          id \"LDP-0001\", load_case, ordered_hops[],\n                        terminates_at (optional)\n                        The candidate is NOT yours to state: this pass is run\n                        once per candidate and the one you are embodying is\n                        named above, so the path is written against it.\n  assembly_steps[]      id \"ASY-0001\", order_index, body, access_side,\n                        activates[], termination_strategy, path_kind, depends_on[]\n  unresolved[]          id \"S3U-1001\", decision, why_open, alternatives[],\n                        alternatives_kind, kept_open_by[], blocks[]\n\n  blocked_direction     +X | -X | +Y | -Y | +Z | -Z | NONE\n  provider_body         a body id, not a description\n  configurations        configuration ids where the relation holds\n  blocked_dofs          which of TX TY TZ RX RY RZ the relation removes\n  driver                LOAD | KINEMATIC_NECESSITY | DECLARED_SCENARIO\n  defeat_specification  how a test would defeat this constraint\n  termination_strategy  LATER_BODY_COVER | ROTATION | ELASTICITY | NONE\n  path_kind             RIGID | DEFORMATION_RESOLVED\n  alternatives_kind     ENTITY_REFS | PRINCIPLE_FAMILIES | FREE_TEXT\n\nPHYSICAL REALIZATION\nThis candidate must physically do what the input's PHYSICAL EFFECT OBLIGATIONS\nrequire. Those obligations are candidate-independent: they say WHAT effect must\noccur, between which roles. You say HOW THIS CANDIDATE does it.\n\n  For every effect obligation this candidate realizes, emit a\n  physical_interaction naming the rigid groups between which the effect passes,\n  the effect (TRANSMIT_FORCE | TRANSMIT_MOTION | CONVERT_MOTION | PERMIT_MOTION | PREVENT_MOTION | LOCATE | CONTAIN | METER), and the obligation id it discharges. An interaction\n  TRANSMITS; a joint CONSTRAINS. They are not the same fact and a joint is not a\n  substitute for one.\n\n  For every constraint this candidate relies on, emit a constraint_relation: the\n  retained group, which DOFs it removes, in which configurations, and what\n  DRIVES it (LOAD | KINEMATIC_NECESSITY | DECLARED_SCENARIO). Name what PROVIDES it - a body of this mechanism in\n  provider_body, or, where the reaction is taken outside the product, the\n  declared reaction site in provider_reaction_site. Those are the two kinds of\n  provider there are; the world is not a body. provider_site is a different\n  fact: the interface of this mechanism at which the constraint acts. Do not\n  leave a constraint standing on nothing, and do not report one you have not\n  decided.\n\n  For every load case, emit a load_path: the ordered interfaces the load passes\n  through, and where it terminates. If the load reaches a declared EXTERNAL\n  reaction site, name it in terminates_at. rendered prompt (47905 chars)

The mechanism below is fixed. Add what holds it together, how
loads reach the world, and in what order it goes together.

Do not add or rename bodies, groups, joints, interfaces or configurations. If
something is missing, say so in unresolved.

1. WHAT HOLDS EACH BODY. For each body that must stay where it is put, state
   what stops it, as a constraint_relation below. ONE relation per (retained
   group, blocked direction) - not one per degree of freedom: the pipeline
   expands each relation over the DOFs and the CONFIGURATIONS THE RELATION
   ITSELF NAMES, and over no others. A relation that names no configuration
   therefore holds nowhere, so name them. A mechanism in which nothing is blocked
   is a pile of loose parts.
2. IRRELEVANCE. Only for a DOF that is BOTH unloaded AND unactuated, naming the
   scenario in which that holds. The scenario is an ID from the input, not a
   description; a scenario carrying a load case is not one. Most mechanisms need
   none.
3. LOAD PATHS. Per load case, the ordered hops from where the load is applied,
   through this mechanism, to the reaction site. A HOP IS AN INTERFACE ID - the
   interface that carries the load across that step. Not a body, not a joint: a
   body is what the load passes through, an interface is what carries it from
   one body to the next. Terminate at the reaction site the load case names, and
   if this mechanism does not reach it, leave terminates_at out and say so.
   Never say how much load anything carries.
4. ASSEMBLY ORDER. Which body, from which access side, what it depends on, and
   what retains it once placed. A rigid part pushed straight in leaves the
   reverse direction open, so a body that must stay put needs LATER_BODY_COVER,
   ROTATION or ELASTICITY. NONE is the fourth value and it is not a strategy: it
   says nothing retains this body, which is the right answer for a part that is
   meant to come back out or that no constraint relation holds, and is not an
   answer for a body you have just declared a constraint_relation retains. Every
   body whose group appears as a `retained_group` above needs one of the three.

RESPONSE SCHEMA
Return one JSON object. Emit every key. Use exactly these key names.

  irrelevance[]         rigid_group, configuration, dof[], scenario
  physical_interactions[]
                        id "PHI-0001", groups[], effect, discharges_effect,
                        at_interface (optional), configurations[] (optional)
  constraint_relations[]
                        id "CRL-0001", retained_group, blocked_dofs[],
                        configurations[], driver, blocked_direction (optional),
                        provider_body (optional),
                        provider_reaction_site (optional),
                        provider_site (optional),
                        maintaining_interaction (optional),
                        defeat_specification (optional)
                        AT LEAST ONE of provider_body / provider_reaction_site
                        must identify what provides the constraint.
                        provider_site is where it acts and does not answer that.
  load_paths[]          id "LDP-0001", load_case, ordered_hops[],
                        terminates_at (optional)
                        The candidate is NOT yours to state: this pass is run
                        once per candidate and the one you are embodying is
                        named above, so the path is written against it.
  assembly_steps[]      id "ASY-0001", order_index, body, access_side,
                        activates[], termination_strategy, path_kind, depends_on[]
  unresolved[]          id "S3U-1001", decision, why_open, alternatives[],
                        alternatives_kind, kept_open_by[], blocks[]

  blocked_direction     +X | -X | +Y | -Y | +Z | -Z | NONE
  provider_body         a body id, not a description
  configurations        configuration ids where the relation holds
  blocked_dofs          which of TX TY TZ RX RY RZ the relation removes
  driver                LOAD | KINEMATIC_NECESSITY | DECLARED_SCENARIO
  defeat_specification  how a test would defeat this constraint
  termination_strategy  LATER_BODY_COVER | ROTATION | ELASTICITY | NONE
  path_kind             RIGID | DEFORMATION_RESOLVED
  alternatives_kind     ENTITY_REFS | PRINCIPLE_FAMILIES | FREE_TEXT

PHYSICAL REALIZATION
This candidate must physically do what the input's PHYSICAL EFFECT OBLIGATIONS
require. Those obligations are candidate-independent: they say WHAT effect must
occur, between which roles. You say HOW THIS CANDIDATE does it.

  For every effect obligation this candidate realizes, emit a
  physical_interaction naming the rigid groups between which the effect passes,
  the effect (TRANSMIT_FORCE | TRANSMIT_MOTION | CONVERT_MOTION | PERMIT_MOTION | PREVENT_MOTION | LOCATE | CONTAIN | METER), and the obligation id it discharges. An interaction
  TRANSMITS; a joint CONSTRAINS. They are not the same fact and a joint is not a
  substitute for one.

  For every constraint this candidate relies on, emit a constraint_relation: the
  retained group, which DOFs it removes, in which configurations, and what
  DRIVES it (LOAD | KINEMATIC_NECESSITY | DECLARED_SCENARIO). Name what PROVIDES it - a body of this mechanism in
  provider_body, or, where the reaction is taken outside the product, the
  declared reaction site in provider_reaction_site. Those are the two kinds of
  provider there are; the world is not a body. provider_site is a different
  fact: the interface of this mechanism at which the constraint acts. Do not
  leave a constraint standing on nothing, and do not report one you have not
  decided.

  For every load case, emit a load_path: the ordered interfaces the load passes
  through, and where it terminates. If the load reaches a declared EXTERNAL
  reaction site, name it in terminates_at. If it does not, leave terminates_at

    "prompt_text": "The mechanism below is fixed. Add what holds it together, how\nloads reach the world, and in what order it goes together.\n\nDo not add or rename bodies, groups, joints, interfaces or configurations. If\nsomething is missing, say so in unresolved.\n\n1. WHAT HOLDS EACH BODY. For each body that must stay where it is put, state\n   what stops it, as a constraint_relation below. rendered prompt (43597 chars)

The mechanism below is fixed. Add what holds it together, how
loads reach the world, and in what order it goes together.

Do not add or rename bodies, groups, joints, interfaces or configurations. If
something is missing, say so in unresolved.

1. WHAT HOLDS EACH BODY. For each body that must stay where it is put, state
   what stops it, as a constraint_relation below. ONE relation per (retained
   group, blocked direction) - not one per degree of freedom: the pipeline
   expands each relation over the DOFs and the CONFIGURATIONS THE RELATION
   ITSELF NAMES, and over no others. A relation that names no configuration
   therefore holds nowhere, so name them. A mechanism in which nothing is blocked
   is a pile of loose parts.
2. IRRELEVANCE. Only for a DOF that is BOTH unloaded AND unactuated, naming the
   scenario in which that holds. The scenario is an ID from the input, not a
   description; a scenario carrying a load case is not one. Most mechanisms need
   none.
3. LOAD PATHS. Per load case, the ordered hops from where the load is applied,
   through this mechanism, to the reaction site. A HOP IS AN INTERFACE ID - the
   interface that carries the load across that step. Not a body, not a joint: a
   body is what the load passes through, an interface is what carries it from
   one body to the next. Terminate at the reaction site the load case names, and
   if this mechanism does not reach it, leave terminates_at out and say so.
   Never say how much load anything carries.
4. ASSEMBLY ORDER. Which body, from which access side, what it depends on, and
   what retains it once placed. A rigid part pushed straight in leaves the
   reverse direction open, so a body that must stay put needs LATER_BODY_COVER,
   ROTATION or ELASTICITY. NONE is the fourth value and it is not a strategy: it
   says nothing retains this body, which is the right answer for a part that is
   meant to come back out or that no constraint relation holds, and is not an
   answer for a body you have just declared a constraint_relation retains. Every
   body whose group appears as a `retained_group` above needs one of the three.

RESPONSE SCHEMA
Return one JSON object. Emit every key. Use exactly these key names.

  irrelevance[]         rigid_group, configuration, dof[], scenario
  physical_interactions[]
                        id "PHI-0001", groups[], effect, discharges_effect,
                        at_interface (optional), configurations[] (optional)
  constraint_relations[]
                        id "CRL-0001", retained_group, blocked_dofs[],
                        configurations[], driver, blocked_direction (optional),
                        provider_body (optional),
                        provider_reaction_site (optional),
                        provider_site (optional),
                        maintaining_interaction (optional),
                        defeat_specification (optional)
                        AT LEAST ONE of provider_body / provider_reaction_site
                        must identify what provides the constraint.
                        provider_site is where it acts and does not answer that.
  load_paths[]          id "LDP-0001", load_case, ordered_hops[],
                        terminates_at (optional)
                        The candidate is NOT yours to state: this pass is run
                        once per candidate and the one you are embodying is
                        named above, so the path is written against it.
  assembly_steps[]      id "ASY-0001", order_index, body, access_side,
                        activates[], termination_strategy, path_kind, depends_on[]
  unresolved[]          id "S3U-1001", decision, why_open, alternatives[],
                        alternatives_kind, kept_open_by[], blocks[]

  blocked_direction     +X | -X | +Y | -Y | +Z | -Z | NONE
  provider_body         a body id, not a description
  configurations        configuration ids where the relation holds
  blocked_dofs          which of TX TY TZ RX RY RZ the relation removes
  driver                LOAD | KINEMATIC_NECESSITY | DECLARED_SCENARIO
  defeat_specification  how a test would defeat this constraint
  termination_strategy  LATER_BODY_COVER | ROTATION | ELASTICITY | NONE
  path_kind             RIGID | DEFORMATION_RESOLVED
  alternatives_kind     ENTITY_REFS | PRINCIPLE_FAMILIES | FREE_TEXT

PHYSICAL REALIZATION
This candidate must physically do what the input's PHYSICAL EFFECT OBLIGATIONS
require. Those obligations are candidate-independent: they say WHAT effect must
occur, between which roles. You say HOW THIS CANDIDATE does it.

  For every effect obligation this candidate realizes, emit a
  physical_interaction naming the rigid groups between which the effect passes,
  the effect (TRANSMIT_FORCE | TRANSMIT_MOTION | CONVERT_MOTION | PERMIT_MOTION | PREVENT_MOTION | LOCATE | CONTAIN | METER), and the obligation id it discharges. An interaction
  TRANSMITS; a joint CONSTRAINS. They are not the same fact and a joint is not a
  substitute for one.

  For every constraint this candidate relies on, emit a constraint_relation: the
  retained group, which DOFs it removes, in which configurations, and what
  DRIVES it (LOAD | KINEMATIC_NECESSITY | DECLARED_SCENARIO). Name what PROVIDES it - a body of this mechanism in
  provider_body, or, where the reaction is taken outside the product, the
  declared reaction site in provider_reaction_site. Those are the two kinds of
  provider there are; the world is not a body. provider_site is a different
  fact: the interface of this mechanism at which the constraint acts. Do not
  leave a constraint standing on nothing, and do not report one you have not
  decided.

  For every load case, emit a load_path: the ordered interfaces the load passes
  through, and where it terminates. If the load reaches a declared EXTERNAL
  reaction site, name it in terminates_at. If it does not, leave terminates_at
  out - an open path is a real answer and saying so is better than closing it
  with something you did not establish.

Every reference above is an ID. A description is not an id, and an interaction
you describe instead of emitting does not exist.

Ids you emit are new. Never reuse an id from the input.

The mechanism below is fixed. Add what holds it together, how
loads reach the world, and in what order it goes together.

Do not add or rename bodies, groups, joints, interfaces or configurations. If
something is missing, say so in unresolved.

1. WHAT HOLDS EACH BODY. For each body that must stay where it is put, state
   what stops it, as a constraint_relation below. ONE relation per (retained
   group, blocked direction) - not one per degree of freedom: the pipeline
   expands each relation over the DOFs and the CONFIGURATIONS THE RELATION
   ITSELF NAMES, and over no others. A relation that names no configuration
   therefore holds nowhere, so name them. A mechanism in which nothing is blocked
   is a pile of loose parts.
2. IRRELEVANCE. Only for a DOF that is BOTH unloaded AND unactuated, naming the
   scenario in which that holds. The scenario is an ID from the input, not a
   description; a scenario carrying a load case is not one. Most mechanisms need
   none.
3. LOAD PATHS. Per load case, the ordered hops from where the load is applied,
   through this mechanism, to the reaction site. A HOP IS AN INTERFACE ID - the
   interface that carries the load across that step. Not a body, not a joint: a
   body is what the load passes through, an interface is what carries it from
   one body to the next. Terminate at the reaction site the load case names, and
   if this mechanism does not reach it, leave terminates_at out and say so.
   Never say how much load anything carries.
4. ASSEMBLY ORDER. Which body, from which access side, what it depends on, and
   what retains it once placed. A rigid part pushed straight in leaves the
   reverse direction open, so a body that must stay put needs LATER_BODY_COVER,
   ROTATION or ELASTICITY. NONE is the fourth value and it is not a strategy: it
   says nothing retains this body, which is the right answer for a part that is
   meant to come back out or that no constraint relation holds, and is not an
   answer for a body you have just declared a constraint_relation retains. Every
   body whose group appears as a `retained_group` above needs one of the three.

RESPONSE SCHEMA
Return one JSON object. Emit every key. Use exactly these key names.

  irrelevance[]         rigid_group, configuration, dof[], scenario
  physical_interactions[]
                        id "PHI-0001", groups[], effect, discharges_effect,
                        at_interface (optional), configurations[] (optional)
  constraint_relations[]
                        id "CRL-0001", retained_group, blocked_dofs[],
                        configurations[], driver, blocked_direction (optional),
                        provider_body (optional),
                        provider_reaction_site (optional),
                        provider_site (optional),
                        maintaining_interaction (optional),
                        defeat_specification (optional)
                        AT LEAST ONE of provider_body / provider_reaction_site
                        must identify what provides the constraint.
                        provider_site is where it acts and does not answer that.
  load_paths[]          id "LDP-0001", load_case, ordered_hops[],
                        terminates_at (optional)
                        The candidate is NOT yours to state: this pass is run
                        once per candidate and the one you are embodying is
                        named above, so the path is written against it.
  assembly_steps[]      id "ASY-0001", order_index, body, access_side,
                        activates[], termination_strategy, path_kind, depends_on[]
  unresolved[]          id "S3U-1001", decision, why_open, alternatives[],
                        alternatives_kind, kept_open_by[], blocks[]

  blocked_direction     +X | -X | +Y | -Y | +Z | -Z | NONE
  provider_body         a body id, not a description
  configurations        configuration ids where the relation holds
  blocked_dofs          which of TX TY TZ RX RY RZ the relation removes
  driver                LOAD | KINEMATIC_NECESSITY | DECLARED_SCENARIO
  defeat_specification  how a test would defeat this constraint
  termination_strategy  LATER_BODY_COVER | ROTATION | ELASTICITY | NONE
  path_kind             RIGID | DEFORMATION_RESOLVED
  alternatives_kind     ENTITY_REFS | PRINCIPLE_FAMILIES | FREE_TEXT

PHYSICAL REALIZATION
This candidate must physically do what the input's PHYSICAL EFFECT OBLIGATIONS
require. Those obligations are candidate-independent: they say WHAT effect must
occur, between which roles. You say HOW THIS CANDIDATE does it.

  For every effect obligation this candidate realizes, emit a
  physical_interaction naming the rigid groups between which the effect passes,
  the effect (TRANSMIT_FORCE | TRANSMIT_MOTION | CONVERT_MOTION | PERMIT_MOTION | PREVENT_MOTION | LOCATE | CONTAIN | METER), and the obligation id it discharges. An interaction
  TRANSMITS; a joint CONSTRAINS. They are not the same fact and a joint is not a
  substitute for one.

  For every constraint this candidate relies on, emit a constraint_relation: the
  retained group, which DOFs it removes, in which configurations, and what
  DRIVES it (LOAD | KINEMATIC_NECESSITY | DECLARED_SCENARIO). Name what PROVIDES it - a body of this mechanism in
  provider_body, or, where the reaction is taken outside the product, the
  declared reaction site in provider_reaction_site. Those are the two kinds of
  provider there are; the world is not a body. provider_site is a different
  fact: the interface of this mechanism at which the constraint acts. Do not
  leave a constraint standing on nothing, and do not report one you have not
  decided.

  For every load case, emit a load_path: the ordered interfaces the load passes
  through, and where it terminates. If the load reaches a declared EXTERNAL
  reaction site, name it in terminates_at. If it does not, leave terminates_at
  out - an open path is a real answer and saying so is better than closing it
  with something you did not establish.

Every reference above is an ID. A description is not an id, and an interaction
you describe instead of emitting does not exist.

Ids you emit are new. Never reuse an id from the input.

These entities already exist in the design state. The ids are listed
so you do not reuse one: every id you emit must be new. This is an
identity list and nothing more - it says which ids are taken, not
what those entities say, and it is not something to reason from.
The example ids in the response schema show the FORMAT of an id.
They are not offers of an available id, and the first index is
commonly the one already taken.

The mechanism below is fixed. Add what holds it together, how
loads reach the world, and in what order it goes together.

Do not add or rename bodies, groups, joints, interfaces or configurations. If
something is missing, say so in unresolved.

1. WHAT HOLDS EACH BODY. For each body that must stay where it is put, state
   what stops it, as a constraint_relation below. ONE relation per (retained
   group, blocked direction) - not one per degree of freedom: the pipeline
   expands each relation over the DOFs and the CONFIGURATIONS THE RELATION
   ITSELF NAMES, and over no others. A relation that names no configuration
   therefore holds nowhere, so name them. A mechanism in which nothing is blocked
   is a pile of loose parts.
2. IRRELEVANCE. Only for a DOF that is BOTH unloaded AND unactuated, naming the
   scenario in which that holds. The scenario is an ID from the input, not a
   description; a scenario carrying a load case is not one. Most mechanisms need
   none.
3. LOAD PATHS. Per load case, the ordered hops from where the load is applied,
   through this mechanism, to the reaction site. A HOP IS AN INTERFACE ID - the
   interface that carries the load across that step. Not a body, not a joint: a
   body is what the load passes through, an interface is what carries it from
   one body to the next. Terminate at the reaction site the load case names, and
   if this mechanism does not reach it, leave terminates_at out and say so.
   Never say how much load anything carries.
4. ASSEMBLY ORDER. Which body, from which access side, what it depends on, and
   what retains it once placed. A rigid part pushed straight in leaves the
   reverse direction open, so a body that must stay put needs LATER_BODY_COVER,
   ROTATION or ELASTICITY. NONE is the fourth value and it is not a strategy: it
   says nothing retains this body, which is the right answer for a part that is
   meant to come back out or that no constraint relation holds, and is not an
   answer for a body you have just declared a constraint_relation retains. Every
   body whose group appears as a `retained_group` above needs one of the three.

RESPONSE SCHEMA
Return one JSON object. Emit every key. Use exactly these key names.

  irrelevance[]         rigid_group, configuration, dof[], scenario
  physical_interactions[]
                        id "PHI-0001", groups[], effect, discharges_effect,
                        at_interface (optional), configurations[] (optional)
  constraint_relations[]
                        id "CRL-0001", retained_group, blocked_dofs[],
                        configurations[], driver, blocked_direction (optional),
                        provider_body (optional),
                        provider_reaction_site (optional),
                        provider_site (optional),
                        maintaining_interaction (optional),
                        defeat_specification (optional)
                        AT LEAST ONE of provider_body / provider_reaction_site
                        must identify what provides the constraint.
                        provider_site is where it acts and does not answer that.
  load_paths[]          id "LDP-0001", load_case, ordered_hops[],
                        terminates_at (optional)
                        The candidate is NOT yours to state: this pass is run
                        once per candidate and the one you are embodying is
                        named above, so the path is written against it.
  assembly_steps[]      id "ASY-0001", order_index, body, access_side,
                        activates[], termination_strategy, path_kind, depends_on[]
  unresolved[]          id "S3U-1001", decision, why_open, alternatives[],
                        alternatives_kind, kept_open_by[], blocks[]

  blocked_direction     +X | -X | +Y | -Y | +Z | -Z | NONE
  provider_body         a body id, not a description
  configurations        configuration ids where the relation holds
  blocked_dofs          which of TX TY TZ RX RY RZ the relation removes
  driver                LOAD | KINEMATIC_NECESSITY | DECLARED_SCENARIO
  defeat_specification  how a test would defeat this constraint
  termination_strategy  LATER_BODY_COVER | ROTATION | ELASTICITY | NONE
  path_kind             RIGID | DEFORMATION_RESOLVED
  alternatives_kind     ENTITY_REFS | PRINCIPLE_FAMILIES | FREE_TEXT

PHYSICAL REALIZATION
This candidate must physically do what the input's PHYSICAL EFFECT OBLIGATIONS
require. Those obligations are candidate-independent: they say WHAT effect must
occur, between which roles. You say HOW THIS CANDIDATE does it.

  For every effect obligation this candidate realizes, emit a
  physical_interaction naming the rigid groups between which the effect passes,
  the effect (TRANSMIT_FORCE | TRANSMIT_MOTION | CONVERT_MOTION | PERMIT_MOTION | PREVENT_MOTION | LOCATE | CONTAIN | METER), and the obligation id it discharges. An interaction
  TRANSMITS; a joint CONSTRAINS. They are not the same fact and a joint is not a
  substitute for one.

  For every constraint this candidate relies on, emit a constraint_relation: the
  retained group, which DOFs it removes, in which configurations, and what
  DRIVES it (LOAD | KINEMATIC_NECESSITY | DECLARED_SCENARIO). Name what PROVIDES it - a body of this mechanism in
  provider_body, or, where the reaction is taken outside the product, the
  declared reaction site in provider_reaction_site. Those are the two kinds of
  provider there are; the world is not a body. provider_site is a different
  fact: the interface of this mechanism at which the constraint acts. Do not
  leave a constraint standing on nothing, and do not report one you have not
  decided.

  For every load case, emit a load_path: the ordered interfaces the load passes
  through, and where it terminates. If the load reaches a declared EXTERNAL
  reaction site, name it in terminates_at. If it does not, leave terminates_at
  out - an open path is a real answer and saying so is better than closing it
  with something you did not establish.

Every reference above is an ID. A description is not an id, and an interaction
you describe instead of emitting does not exist.

Ids you emit are new. Never reuse an id from the input.
